episodes.summary: On Thursday, Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia's president, chief executive and board member. CFO Colette Kress is now interim CEO and keeps the CFO title, and Harvey Jones became the company's first-ever board chair. Those mechanics have been well aired.

episodes.title: Enterprise Technology & Software — November 16, 2026
episodes.summary: The per-seat license is being squeezed from both ends at once. ServiceNow is pointing AI at the cost of leaving a rival's installed base. At the same time, it is moving its own revenue away from seats. So far, the evidence for both is a limited launch and a ratio, not a single displaced customer.

episodes.title: Robotics & Physical AI — November 16, 2026
episodes.summary: Yesterday we closed on one line. If the brain thesis holds, value migrates toward the body, and nobody has priced the body yet. Today we can at least start counting the bodies. These are the first shipment tallies this desk has had, and they show where the bodies are built.

episodes.title: Space & the Orbital Economy — November 16, 2026
episodes.summary: All week this desk has asked one question. Who, besides SpaceX, can turn money into a sustained launch cadence? This weekend produced two answers. One is a clean yes, at small scale. The other was the heavy-lift test, and it now looks like a no.

episodes.title: Private Credit & the Corporate Credit Cycle — November 16, 2026
episodes.summary: All week this desk has tracked one direction of traffic: risk moving from banks to non-banks. A failed syndication pushed Fullscript's buyout financing toward private lenders. ING put data-center loans up for sale to private credit and insurers.

episodes.title: Private Equity & the Deal Economy — November 16, 2026
episodes.summary: On Thursday, we told you North American exit counts were on pace for a record year. We also flagged what that data didn't give us: a dollar value. The value data is now in. It tells a meaningfully different story, and it means revising our own read.

episodes.title: The Throughline (daily synthesis) — November 16, 2026
episodes.summary: Today's headline: days before its shares are due to price, Anthropic's IPO filing says the company has met its safety-policy threshold for AI accelerating AI research, judged on a forecast rather than a measurement.

episodes.title: The Forward Curve (daily forecast) (Experimental) — November 16, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the scorecard. Nothing came due over the weekend. But one call moved hard against me, and another moved a little.

episodes.title: Frontier AI Lab Competition — November 17, 2026
episodes.summary: One standing disclosure before we start. Anthropic makes the model behind this show, and today's lead story is Anthropic's own securities filing.

episodes.title: Capital Markets Cross-Asset Radar — November 17, 2026
episodes.summary: The thesis today is simple. On Monday, the broad index finally paid the discount-rate bill that bonds, gold, Bitcoin and Nvidia had been paying all week. And Nvidia's chip peers fell harder than Nvidia itself.

episodes.title: Digital Money, Crypto, and Market Structure — November 17, 2026
episodes.summary: Yesterday's first watch item was Monday's spot bitcoin ETF session, and whether the seven-day outflow streak would break. That print isn't in hand this morning. So I can't tell you whether the streak broke or extended, and I won't guess. What's new today is a different question.

episodes.title: Strategic Power, Energy, and Institutional Change — November 17, 2026
episodes.summary: Today's through-line is that economic statecraft is moving its perimeter outward. Washington and Brussels are both reaching past the adversary to the middlemen who move chips and oil. Beijing is answering with a lever that needs no middleman at all.

episodes.title: Semiconductors & Compute Infrastructure — November 17, 2026
episodes.summary: The headline is a new Commerce Department rule on AI compute, reported Monday, and it's a bigger deal than it sounds. The control point in US export policy just moved. The old regime asked where a chip shipped.

episodes.title: Enterprise Technology & Software — November 17, 2026
episodes.summary: One standing disclosure before we start. Anthropic makes the model behind this show, and it's also today's lead story, so listen with that in mind.

episodes.title: Robotics & Physical AI — November 17, 2026
episodes.summary: All last week this desk asked one question about embodied intelligence. If the robot brain commoditizes, who captures the value? The brain, the body, or whoever owns the storefront in front of both? Over the past five days, robotaxis gave an unusually concrete answer.

episodes.title: Space & the Orbital Economy — November 17, 2026
episodes.summary: Yesterday this desk could only report the Vulcan loss through unconfirmed headlines. Today it's confirmed. And the story is bigger than Amazon.

episodes.title: The Throughline (daily synthesis) — November 17, 2026
episodes.summary: Today's headline: Anthropic's amended IPO filing gives the frontier AI race its first filed profit-and-loss statement, and it lands the day before the company prices its shares.

episodes.title: The Forward Curve (daily forecast) (Experimental) — November 17, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the scorecard. Nothing resolved overnight. One call comes due tonight, and one past hit now faces a conflicting read.
